Planning the shape first: apex-at-origin bevel pair, pinion on +x, wheel on +z, both pitch cones tangent along a line in the x–z plane. Teeth built as an apex-projection of a planar involute profile (standard straight-bevel CAD approximation), thinned by half the backlash each. Cell 1 just fixes and prints the parameters.

```python
import numpy as np, build123d as bd, math, os, subprocess
os.makedirs("constant/triSurface", exist_ok=True)

# ---- given by the request ----
m      = 3.0        # module, mm
Np, Nw = 20, 30     # teeth
alpha  = math.radians(20.0)
B      = 0.3        # backlash along pitch line, mm (total)
LX, LY, LZ = 160.0, 140.0, 120.0   # cavity, mm
SIGMA  = 90.0       # shaft angle, deg

# ---- derived bevel geometry ----
gp = math.atan2(Np, Nw); gw = math.atan2(Nw, Np)     # pitch cone half angles
rp, rw = m*Np/2, m*Nw/2                              # outer pitch radii
A0 = rp/math.sin(gp)
print(f"pitch dia  pinion {2*rp:.3f} mm   wheel {2*rw:.3f} mm")
print(f"cone angles {math.degrees(gp):.3f} + {math.degrees(gw):.3f} = {math.degrees(gp+gw):.3f} deg (target {SIGMA})")
print(f"outer cone distance A0 = {A0:.4f} mm  (check {rw/math.sin(gw):.4f})")
print(f"circular pitch p = {math.pi*m:.4f} mm, tooth thickness each = {math.pi*m/2 - B/2:.4f} mm")
print("build123d", bd.__version__)
```

*(chosen, not given: face width, hub/shaft/bore sizes — set next cell)*

Now the tooth profile generator and the pinion solid. Teeth are the apex-projection (ruled loft) of a planar involute profile; tip/root radii come from ±addendum/dedendum measured perpendicular to the pitch cone, projected onto the outer plane.

Re-emitting self-contained (the earlier definitions came from an errored cell). Also verifying the face/root cone angles against γ±δ, which is what fixes addendum = 3 mm and dedendum = 3.75 mm perpendicular to the pitch cone.

The flat outer/inner faces stick out past the back and front cones, so the tooth corners of the two gears touch. Fixing it the faithful way: trim the toothed band by the back cone and front cone (both perpendicular to the pitch cone), and add the core frustum back so the body stays solid.

Boolean with the 30-tooth loft returns None, so first a quick robustness probe, and switching the trim to spheres about the common apex (trimming at constant cone distance guarantees the two gears cannot interfere).

The loft was self-intersecting: the axis-normal-plane profile gives pointed teeth on the wheel. The correct construction is Tredgold's — draw the involute on the back-cone development (equivalent spur gear radius r/cos γ, azimuth compressed by cos γ), then project from the apex. Trims become spheres about the common apex, so both gears live in the same shell Ai<A<A0 and cannot interfere.
The polyline ordering was wrong — teeth were being joined tip-to-tip instead of across the root land, which is what made the loft self-intersecting. Fixed and re-plotted:
Now the gear solids: apex-projection loft trimmed by spheres of radius A0 and Ai (constant cone distance), plus core, hub and shaft.
